item.title: QVS chasing national success
item.description: QUEEN Victoria School’s (QVS) under-18 title hopes may have ended at the national quarter-final stage, but the school’s wider campaign remains alive with four teams through to the semi-finals of the Vodafone Super Deans Competition. QVS will contest the U14, U15, U16 and U17 semi-finals this week, giving the school four opportunities to reach the national finals.
item.content:encoded:
QUEEN Victoria School’s (QVS) under-18 title hopes may have ended at the national quarter-final stage, but the school’s wider campaign remains alive with four teams through to the semi-finals of the Vodafone Super Deans Competition.

QVS will contest the U14, U15, U16 and U17 semi-finals this week, giving the school four opportunities to reach the national finals.

The continued presence of the four teams reflects the broader approach outlined by QVS principal Wailiki Nasau before the national knockout stages, when he said the school’s focus was no longer limited to success in the Eastern Zone.

“The focus now is not only like, you know, to be to the zone only, it’s our road to the national quota,” Nasau said.

He said QVS had also taken its preparation to another level compared with last year as the school looked to meet the growing standard of secondary school rugby across the country.

The U14 side will face Mahatma Ghandi Memorial School at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, while the U15 team meets Ratu Kadavulevu School at the same venue.

In the U16 grade, QVS faces Marist Brothers High School, while the U17 side takes on Suva Grammar School, both at HFC Bank Stadium.

For QVS, the four semi-final appearances provide an opportunity to turn its wider national ambitions into results, despite the early exit of its U18 side.

item.title: Komo maintains winning run against Nadi
item.description: KOMO’S winning run in the Super 8 Championship continued at Albert Park yesterday, with a four-wicket victory over Nadi giving the side another boost in Pool B. Nadi batted first and posted 117 runs for the loss of nine wickets, setting Komo a target of 118 runs.
item.content:encoded:
KOMO’S winning run in the Super 8 Championship continued at Albert Park yesterday, with a four-wicket victory over Nadi giving the side another boost in Pool B.

Nadi batted first and posted 117 runs for the loss of nine wickets, setting Komo a target of 118 runs.

Komo responded confidently, reaching 118 for six wickets in 25 overs to complete the chase and claim another valuable victory.

Vice-captain Waisea Rabuli praised his teammates for their effort but said the match also gave the side important lessons to take forward.

“We could put in more effort in the field,” Rabuli said.

He said the game highlighted areas Komo could improve as they continue their campaign.

“It showed a lot on the field, the weaknesses in our fielding,” he said.

Despite those concerns, Rabuli was pleased with the way the team handled Nadi’s challenge and credited their opponents for making the match competitive.

“Nadi gave a good score for us to beat,” he said.

The vice-captain was also grateful for the commitment shown by his teammates throughout the contest.

“Grateful for the boys’ effort,” Rabuli said.

He also acknowledged Nadi for the challenge they provided.

“Grateful for Nadi for putting up a good match,” he said. The victory moved Komo to four points in Pool B after they opened their campaign with a win over Suva on the first day, earning two points.

The result gives Komo confidence heading into the next stage of their pool campaign, while also providing areas for the team to work on.

Komo will now face Ono-i-Lau today at 12.30pm, with another opportunity to strengthen their position and continue their positive start.

For Rabuli and his teammates, the focus will be on building from the positives of the Nadi victory while tightening up the areas that need attention.

The successful chase showed Komo’s ability to respond under pressure, while their fielding performance has given the side a clear area to improve before their next match. With another challenge ahead, Komo will be looking to carry their confidence, teamwork and determination into today’s encounter as they continue their push in the Super 8 Championship.

item.title: Schools use inter-house to develop young talent
item.description: FOR the young athletes of Dilkusha Boys’ and Dilkusha Girls’ Primary School, the annual inter-house athletics meet was more than a day of competition, it was an opportunity to take the first step towards a bigger sporting stage. item.content:encoded:
FOR the young athletes of Dilkusha Boys’ and Dilkusha Girls’ Primary School, the annual inter-house athletics meet was more than a day of competition, it was an opportunity to take the first step towards a bigger sporting stage.

The event brought together students from Years 4 to 8, giving them a platform to test their abilities, compete for their houses and catch the attention of those looking for promising young talent.

Head of School at Dilkusha Girls’ Primary School Alani­eta Ratumaimuri said the competition was an important part of the students’ overall development and could provide a pathway towards district and national athletics.

“It is part of the holistic development, where students come and showcase their talents so that they will represent the school into the district meet and then to the national level,” Ratumaimuri said.

She said school competitions such as the inter-house meet allowed students to discover and develop their strengths while preparing them for higher levels of competition.

The pathway is already familiar to Dilkusha, with former students progressing to secondary schools such as Mahtma Gandhi Memorial School and Adi Cakobau School after displaying promise in athletics.

Ratumaimuri said the school hoped more students would follow that path through continued participation, commitment and development.

For her, the role of sport extends well beyond the athletics track.

“With the holistic approach in education, that’s why we are out here. It’s not just confined to the four walls of a classroom,” she said.

She believes identifying sporting talent early can give students opportunities that could extend beyond their school years.

“We want to showcase the talents that our students have so that they can also earn a living in sports, whether it’s in athletics or rugby,” Ratumaimuri said.

With students from both Dilkusha Primary Schools competing, the inter-house meet provided a foundation for the next stage of their sporting journey.

item.title: Podium finishes for Rainibogi, Jasmine
item.description: Rainibogi opened the men’s 110kg snatch with 165kg, missed at 170kg, then took 170kg on his final attempt and reclaimed the Commonwealth Games record England’s Cyrille Tchatchet II had set at 166kg minutes earlier. The clean and jerk followed the same shape. He missed his opener at 203kg and made it second time. Tchatchet II answered with 204kg, then 208kg. Rainibogi loaded 208kg for his last lift
item.content:encoded:
Rainibogi opened the men’s 110kg snatch with 165kg, missed at 170kg, then took 170kg on his final attempt and reclaimed the Commonwealth Games record England’s Cyrille Tchatchet II had set at 166kg minutes earlier.

The clean and jerk followed the same shape. He missed his opener at 203kg and made it second time. Tchatchet II answered with 204kg, then 208kg. Rainibogi loaded 208kg for his last lift, made it, and finished on 378kg. Canada’s Xavier Lusignan then failed at 209kg and the gold was Fiji’s.

Three Commonwealth Games records in one session: the snatch, the clean and jerk and the total. Tchatchet II took silver on 374kg, Lusignan bronze on 356kg. Both Rainibogi and Tchatchet II clean and jerked 208kg. The four kilograms between gold and silver came entirely from the snatch.

What the record sheet doesn’t show is that none of it was his best. He has clean and jerked 211kg and totalled 380kg. His 173kg snatch is an equal Commonwealth record and still stands. Rainibogi won a Commonwealth title, rewrote the Games books three times, and had more in reserve.

He is Fiji’s first Commonwealth Games weightlifting champion since 2018. Four years ago in Birmingham he took bronze at 96kg, beaten by Samoa’s Don Opeloge. This time it was Don’s brother Jack who was expected to challenge. Jack Opeloge failed three times at 210kg and did not finish. “He’s a very experienced lifter, and the other lifters are very strong,” Rainibogi said.

She has been boxing for three years. She was ten when she decided this was what she wanted.

She is now the first woman to represent Fiji in boxing internationally and the first Fijian woman to box at a Commonwealth Games.

She beat Adelaide Dede Djabatey of Ghana 5–0, every judge. In the quarter-final she beat Keshani Hansika of Sri Lanka 4–1, and with that win became the first Fijian woman to secure a boxing medal at a Commonwealth Games. The semi-final brought Michaela Walsh of Northern Ireland, the Birmingham 2022 champion, who won unanimously.

“It’s a bittersweet moment,” Daunakamakama said afterwards. Her coach Cameron Todd hugged her away from the crowd. She told FBC she was grateful for the experience and would come back stronger. Asked what carries her, she talks about mana, the belief shared across Melanesian and Polynesian communities, and describes it as the will to overcome fears that are not real.

David Young became the first Fijian swimmer to reach a Commonwealth Games final, finishing sixth in the 50m Freestyle. Anahira McCutcheon broke the Fiji record in the 100m Freestyle and made three semi-finals. Samuel Yalimaiwai broke the national 50m Breaststroke record. Gerard Takayawa finished seventh in the +100kg judo. Rusiate Matai cleared a season-best 2.05 metres in the High Jump final, and Sitiveni Konataci threw a season-best 27.54 metres in the Men’s Discus F42-44/F61-64 final. Rajnesh Prasad beat a former World Champion on the bowls greens on the first morning of competition. Team Fiji finished 20th, level with the Bahamas and the Isle of Man.

Neither medal belongs to one person. Weightlifting Fiji head coach Henry Elder spoke afterwards about a journey full of obstacles and setbacks, which is the honest description of what sits behind both results. Thank you to the coaches who built these programmes over years, to the team managers who ran three villages and got athletes to the right venue at the right hour, to the medical and support staff, and to Weightlifting Fiji and the Fiji Amateur Boxing Association. And to the families who drove to training before dawn for years so this fortnight could happen.

Thank you also to Glasgow. To the organising committee, the venue staff, and the thousands of volunteers who pointed, translated and cheered through eleven days. Volunteers are the first people athletes remember.

Team Fiji comes home with a gold, a bronze, national records in the pool and a first for Fijian swimming.

Jasmine Daunakamakama (left) with coach Cam Todd. Picture: FASANOC

item.title: Nasinu eye redemption in Deans U18 semi-final
item.description: NASINU Secondary School is one step away from Vodafone Deans Trophy U18 final, but captain Maika Tuivaga knows his side must raise the intensity if they are to get past Lelean Memorial School in Saturday’s semi-final at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva. Nasinu secured a hard-fought 28-26 victory over Cuvu College in their quarter-final at Garvey Park last week to book their place in the final four.
item.content:encoded:
NASINU Secondary School is one step away from Vodafone Deans Trophy U18 final, but captain Maika Tuivaga knows his side must raise the intensity if they are to get past Lelean Memorial School in Saturday’s semi-final at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Nasinu secured a hard-fought 28-26 victory over Cuvu College in their quarter-final at Garvey Park last week to book their place in the final four.

The narrow victory has given the side confidence, but Tuivaga believes there is still plenty of work to be done before they take on their Eastern Zone counterparts.

“We must lift up our preparation for the semi-final and improve on our weaknesses from the quarter-final.

“We also have to encourage my brothers on the field and make sure we stay together as a team,” Tuivaga said.

Reflecting on their quarter-final against Cuvu, Tuivaga said the match exposed areas of their game that needed attention.

“It was a good game in the quarter-final against Cuvu last week, but there are areas we need to improve on, and I know we will do better.”

Nasinu will be hoping to turn last year’s disappointment into motivation as they continue their campaign for the prestigious Deans Trophy.

The school reached the U18 final last year but fell short against defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School.

With another opportunity now in front of them, Tuivaga believes the team must remain focused and disciplined as they chase a place in the final.

The clash against Lelean is expected to be another stern test for Nasinu, with both sides eager to secure a place in the championship decider.

For Tuivaga and his teammates, Saturday’s semi-final is not only about progressing to the final but also another opportunity to move closer to redemption after last year’s heartbreak.

item.title: Lal wins Indra Warjan trophy
item.description: JYOTI Lal was the overall winner of the Indra Warjan Trophy at the Ba Golf Club last weekend, finishing with an impressive net score of 65. The tournament served as the final weekend event for Ba Golf Club ahead of the prestigious RCM Ba Open, which will be held on August 15 and 16.
item.content:encoded:
JYOTI Lal was the overall winner of the Indra Warjan Trophy at the Ba Golf Club last weekend, finishing with an impressive net score of 65.

The tournament served as the final weekend event for Ba Golf Club ahead of the prestigious RCM Ba Open, which will be held on August 15 and 16.

Lal also claimed the nearest-to-the-pin prize on hole three and 12, adding to an impressive outing on the course.

Ashish Chand topped the overall gross category with a score of 70, while Ashwin Sharma secured first place in the A Grade net category with 66.

Sponsor and former Fiji team gold medallist Indra Warjan finished second in the A Grade with 68, while Raven Kumar was third with 73.

In the B Grade, Mohammed Ali took first place with 66, followed by Marshal Pillai on 71 and Brendan Daniel on 71.

Tarun Sewak won the C Grade with 66, while Anaya Saanvi finished second with 69 and Ravinesh Chand third with 72.

Christopher Daniel won the longest drive, while Ali also claimed the second-best shot prize.

The Ba Golf Club thanked Warjan, along with its officials, volunteers, match committee, starters, card officials and members for contributing to the success of the tournament.

Attention now turns to the RCM Ba Open this weekend, with golfers expected to converge on the Ba Golf Club for the two-day tournament.

item.title: Gounder, McCarthy claim championship honours
item.description: CHAMPIONSHIP pressure, consistency and shot-making were put to the test over last weekend as members battled across 36 holes for honours at the 2026 Fiji Golf Club Championship. The two-day tournament brought together golfers across the A, B and C grades, as well as the women’s divisions, with players competing in a stroke event without handicap advantages.
item.content:encoded:
CHAMPIONSHIP pressure, consistency and shot-making were put to the test over last weekend as members battled across 36 holes for honours at the 2026 Fiji Golf Club Championship.

The two-day tournament brought together golfers across the A, B and C grades, as well as the women’s divisions, with players competing in a stroke event without handicap advantages.

When the final scores were tallied, Ravinesh Gounder emerged as the men’s champion with a gross score of 154, while Merelita McCarthy claimed the women’s title with a gross score of 163.

The championship provided a stern test for members, with every shot counting as golfers worked to produce their best performances across the two rounds.

Championship Chairman Alex Konrote said the event remained one of the club’s most significant tournaments, providing members with an opportunity to compete for honours while also serving as a pathway towards higher-level golf.

“The Fiji Golf Club Championship is meant only for the members and it’s a two-day tournament which is a qualifier for the club champion in your respective grades,” Konrote said.

The championship was played over 36 holes, with gross scores determining the standings and the players progressing through the various stages of the competition.

Konrote said the format placed the focus firmly on each golfer’s ability rather than handicap advantage.

“Basically today (Saturday) you’re in your grades but you’re not playing your handicap, you’re just playing exactly how good you are of the stick,” he said.

Beyond the battle for club honours, the championship also provides an important development opportunity for golfers looking to progress to higher levels of the sport.

Konrote said the tournament has helped provide a pathway for players with ambitions of representing Fiji.

“It is a stepping-stone if you’re looking for, if you’re vying for national qualification,” he said.

The weekend’s competition once again highlighted the depth of talent within the Fiji Golf Club, while giving members valuable experience under championship conditions.

With Gounder and McCarthy securing the major honours, the 2026 championship has provided another platform for the club’s golfers to test themselves and continue their pursuit of higher honours.

item.title: Raiders sharpen their title chase
item.description: USP Raiders under-17 captain Tony Vakaloloma believes last Saturday’s 18-0 victory over Makoi Bulldogs can provide the platform for another strong campaign in the Vodafone Cup Eastern State Rugby League Clubs Competition. The Round Seven clash at the USP Grounds saw the Raiders produce a disciplined defensive display, keeping Makoi scoreless from start to finish.
item.content:encoded:
USP Raiders under-17 captain Tony Vakaloloma believes last Saturday’s 18-0 victory over Makoi Bulldogs can provide the platform for another strong campaign in the Vodafone Cup Eastern State Rugby League Clubs Competition.

The Round Seven clash at the USP Grounds saw the Raiders produce a disciplined defensive display, keeping Makoi scoreless from start to finish.

For Vakaloloma, the result was a reflection of the collective effort within the side.

“It was a good team effort,” Vakaloloma said.

The Raiders know what it takes to go deep into the competition.

Last year, they fought their way through to the final but fell short of claiming the title, an experience that has added motivation to their campaign this season.

Vakaloloma believes the lessons from that disappointment can help the young side handle the pressure as the competition progresses.

“We just have to look ahead to the next matches,” he said.

That focus was evident against Makoi, with the Raiders refusing to let their intensity drop and maintaining their defensive structure throughout the match.

The clean sheet was one of the biggest positives from the Round Seven outing, with Makoi unable to breach the Raiders’ defence.

Vakaloloma praised his teammates for working together and staying committed to their roles, saying the result came from a collective effort rather than individual performances.

With last year’s final appearance still fresh in their minds, the Raiders are determined to make the experience count this season.

The 18-0 victory provides confidence, but Vakaloloma knows the road ahead will demand consistency.

The captain is urging his teammates to remain focused, continue improving and carry the same discipline into their upcoming matches.

For the Raiders, the goal is no longer simply to reach the final.
